decisions.rationale: Accepted (captain decision pep-project-rows, option A, corr=d5079262d537a4a6): the confirmed matrix already includes this project row, so this is one of the 14 already-authorized project artifacts, not new scope. Plan one reusable learner-facing project brief for the row: explicit outcomes, prerequisite alignment, a starter scaffold and public language-native tests. No Docker/Podman/Compose in learner setup; reference solutions and hidden tests stay out of the repository. The same canonical artifact is reused by the Standard and Fast overlays, never duplicated. The intake records the artifact plan (location in the canonical tree, outcomes, prerequisite map, scaffold and test command); the module PR authors it. Every concept the project applies must be taught before the project day: map each one to the earlier topic objective or the in-brief instruction that teaches it, and close any gap in the plan. F10: null/NullPointerException and Maven POM dependency declaration must be taught before F10, in earlier topic objectives or explicit instruction inside the F10 brief, and checked by its public tests.

Rewrite the F7 two-pointer objectives to use already-taught Strings and indexes: build and return a reversed String, count matching characters or pairs, choose the stopping condition. In-place array work moves to F8. Never describe String reversal as in place.
Same correction as education-02: reverse an array in place only once arrays are taught (F8); a String is reversed by building a new result or through a mutable char[]/StringBuilder.

Accepted with a scope limit. The confirmed coverage matrix gives Java no lab overlay, so no lab is added. Narrow the Javalin topic objectives to what the page activity, simulator and quiz can evidence: tracing and selecting routes, handlers and Context use, and predicting responses. Add an optional guided local-run step in the page using the documented offline Maven command. Record the applicability honestly.
Keep F6 on primitive copying and reference-value reassignment with String; leave array mutation transfer to F8 authoring.
Learners inspect a short Java 8, 11 or 17 example, predict whether it compiles on JDK 25 and name the feature or migration issue behind the prediction.
Same as education-05: state that older source often, not always, stays compatible; removed APIs, options and dependencies can break it.

Rewrite o3: String objects are immutable. Inspecting methods return numbers or characters; transformation methods return a String value without changing the receiver. Do not promise a newly allocated object.

Keep the formats and the 45-minute block. Replace one lower-priority MCQ objective with a Javalin route/handler trace objective, and keep only coding objectives the two tasks directly elicit within the time.
Replace the javadoc.io Mockito evidence with the first-party API documentation on site.mockito.org, with a current receipt.
